name: Rippling
summary: Workforce platform that unifies HR, IT and Finance in one system of record: run payroll and benefits, manage hiring, onboarding and time tracking, and provision devices and app access automatically — with policy-driven automation across employee data, approvals and compliance. Three additions the vendor announced during 2026, read on rippling.com on 22 September 2026 and not something we have tested: Helpdesk (announced 1 September), an agent that resolves routine IT requests — app access, password resets, device replacements — through deterministic, admin-approved steps across Rippling's own device, inventory and identity tools; AI Governance (announced 20 August), which breaks AI spend down by employee attribute and governs how staff connect LLMs to other tools; and Data Cloud, an AI-powered BI layer over the same employee record. Check availability before you buy the middle one: on Rippling's own AI Governance page only the AI Spend Console invites you to try it, while the AI Gateway and the discovery of unsanctioned AI use are waitlists and the MCP Gateway routes to sales.
best_for: growing companies that want HR, IT and Finance on one employee record — so a single hire can trigger payroll, a provisioned laptop and app access at once, and offboarding claws it all back automatically
skip_if: you need only one function, like standalone payroll or device management, where a focused and transparently-priced point tool is cheaper and simpler — or you need firm pricing before committing to a sales conversation
honest_knock: The published '$8 per employee a month' is real but it's only the floor, it comes with a monthly base fee ($40 on the small-business page), and it's the HR-and-payroll entry — not the price of the platform. Rippling sells HR, IT and Finance as separate, separately-quoted modules, so you can't comparison-shop without a sales call, and a single-module deployment pays platform prices for a point tool. You're buying a system of record; the value only shows up once you consolidate several systems onto it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per employee a month plus a $40 monthly base fee (published floor)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-16) Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The pricing page is a custom-quote form: you tell it which of HR, IT and Finance you need and your headcount, and a price comes back through sales. What Rippling does publish is a floor. The FAQ on the pricing page says plans start at $8 per employee per month, with a monthly base fee, and that most products are priced per employee per month while some add a monthly base fee. The small-business page names that base fee: 'Starting at $8 per user per month. Plus, a $40 per month base fee.' Whether the same $40 applies to every module and company size is not stated. That floor is an entry point, not a quote; the real bill is quote-based and depends on which modules you switch on and how many employees you run, and Rippling Payroll itself is quote-only. Eligible US VC-backed startups can get 6 months of free access through Rippling's startup program, depending on funding status and stage. Decide the exact module mix you need before you compare vendors, because Rippling's cost scales with how much of it you adopt.

vendor_mcp.what: Built on Code Mode rather than one tool per API: the agent searches a catalog of functions and executes code against them, across HR, IT, Time and Payroll. Rippling puts the token cost of a typical task at 98% below wrapping their 238 APIs as tools.
